root_cause.text: In the ASoC qdsp6/q6apm teardown path, q6apm-audio’s .remove callback ran before its dependent q6apm DAI components, deleting the card’s PCM runtime/RTD structures those components were still linked through and leaving stale component-to-card links that crashed on rebind.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “q6apm-audio .remove callback unloads topology and removes PCM runtimes… This deletes the RTDs that contain the q6apm DAI components before their removal pass runs,” and the patch fixes it by setting explicit component remove ordering: child DAIs to `SND_SOC_COMP_ORDER_FIRST`/`EARLY` and q6apm-audio to `SND_SOC_COMP_ORDER_LAST`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set the q6apm front-end DAI component to remove early so teardown occurs in the correct order during device cleanup.
intent_record.what: A new field initializer was added to the static snd_soc_component_driver instance q6apm_fe_dai_component, setting .remove_order to SND_SOC_COMP_ORDER_EARLY.
intent_record.how: This changes the component's teardown sequence so it is removed in the early removal phase, affecting runtime behavior during device unbind or shutdown by ensuring this component is detached before others that may depend on ordered cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set the LPASS DAI component to be removed first so ASoC teardown happens in the correct order during device cleanup.
intent_record.what: A new field assignment, `.remove_order = SND_SOC_COMP_ORDER_FIRST,`, was added to the `q6apm_lpass_dai_component` `snd_soc_component_driver` structure initializer.
intent_record.how: This changes the component's teardown ordering so it is removed early according to the ASoC component removal order, which can prevent incorrect shutdown sequencing during device removal or cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set the q6apm audio component to be removed last so teardown happens in the correct order during device removal.
intent_record.what: A new field initializer, .remove_order = SND_SOC_COMP_ORDER_LAST, was added to the q6apm_audio_component snd_soc_component_driver structure definition.
intent_record.how: This changes the component driver's teardown sequencing so its remove callback runs in the last removal phase, which can prevent improper shutdown ordering relative to other ASoC components during device removal.

grouping_result.intent: Set the q6apm audio component to be removed last so teardown happens in the correct order during device removal.

consistency_review.core_intent: Adjust the removal ordering of interdependent ASoC audio components so device teardown occurs in the correct sequence during cleanup/removal.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly alter ASoC component removal order so dependent DAI components are torn down before q6apm-audio, which matches the root cause of incorrect teardown sequencing leaving stale links and causing crashes on rebind.

candidates.rationale: The root cause is incorrect teardown ordering: the q6apm audio component's remove callback ran before dependent DAI components, freeing card PCM runtime/RTD structures while stale links still existed. This remove callback registration is the direct statement that enabled the problematic early teardown behavior before the fix added ordering control.

This component definition lacked the pre-remove ordering attribute added by the fix, so it did not get torn down early enough relative to q6apm_audio_remove. While not itself a remove callback, it identifies the affected DAI component instance whose stale links persisted during removal.

Like the other DAI component, this pre-fix component registration lacked the ordering attribute needed to ensure it was removed before q6apm audio. That omission contributed to stale component-to-card links surviving until after PCM runtime teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This registration caused q6apm_audio_remove to participate in the default teardown order, allowing the q6apm audio component to be removed before dependent DAI components. That early remove path deleted the card PCM runtime/RTD structures while stale component-to-card links from the DAI components still existed, leading to crashes on rebind.

commit 5477518b8a0e8a45239646acd80c9bafc4401522
Author: Srinivas Kandagatla <srini@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Oct 26 12:16:48 2021 +0100

    ASoC: qdsp6: audioreach: add q6apm support
    
    Add support to q6apm (Audio Process Manager) component which is
    core Audioreach service running in the DSP.
    
    Signed-off-by: Srinivas Kandagatla <srinivas.kandagatla@linaro.org>
    Reviewed-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/2021102
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows the q6apm ASoC component's remove callback and its registration. The vulnerable construct is present in `static void q6apm_audio_remove(struct snd_soc_component *component)`, which unconditionally does `snd_soc_tplg_component_remove(component);`. The root cause describes that in teardown, q6apm-audio's `.remove` ran before dependent q6apm DAI components, causing topology/card PCM runtime structures to be deleted while other components still referenced them. This initial commit registers that remove hook via `static const struct snd_soc_component_driver q6apm_audio_component = { ... .remove = q6apm_audio_remove, };` and registers the component in `apm_probe()` with `devm_snd_soc_register_component(dev, &q6apm_audio_component, NULL, 0);`. There is no guarding logic, no deferred teardown ordering, and no alternative safe cleanup path in the shown code. Therefore the vulnerable remove-time topology deletion is present, and the fix is not present.
